text:
A peripheral IV cannula is flushed with about 5–10 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride before and after each medicine or fluid, and every 8–12 hours (often once a shift) while unused. A continuous infusion is flushed when the line is accessed. Local IV policy sets the exact interval; some units use a shorter one, and central lines follow a different schedule.
